page: Microsoft Azure D64as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv5 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The instance features 64 dedicated virtual CPUs, mapped from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This configuration does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable, allowing connection to external high-performance block storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieves top 25% results in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, Geekbench multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics simulations. Memory performance is highly competitive, with the Passmark memory score placing in the top 10% tier, and small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth reaching the top 25% tier at 4149.44 GB/sec. However, uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidth falls into the average category.

With its balanced resource allocation and strong multi-threaded capabilities, the D64as_v5 is well-suited for multi-threaded decompression tasks, software compilation, and database operations, as evidenced by its top 25% performance in bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, Geekbench software compilation, and Passmark database operations. It also handles Redis SET operations and small-model LLM inference efficiently. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached Premium Storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy workloads. The instance represents a resource-dense, cost-efficient option for enterprise general-purpose workloads, web serving, and medium-scale database deployments.
